title: New York Islanders Collaborate to Build Child-Designed Playground at Cross Island YMCA
text:
A partnership between the New York Islanders, YMCA, and KABOOM! has resulted in a new community playground designed by local children to promote youth wellness and community ties.
The New York Islanders have demonstrated their commitment to local youth by spearheading a collaborative effort to construct a state-of-the-art community playground. This initiative brought together three major entities: the Islanders Children's Foundation, the YMCA of Greater New York, and the national nonprofit organization known as KABOOM!.
The project culminated in a vibrant new play space located at the YMCA's Hillside Avenue facility, specifically the Cross Island YMCA. By combining resources and manpower, these organizations aimed to create more than just a physical structure; they sought to build a sanctuary for creativity, exercise, and social interaction for children in the surrounding area. The event served as a powerful testament to what can be achieved when professional sports franchises align their goals with community wellness and youth development.
The build day saw a remarkable transformation as New York Islanders players stepped away from their usual routines on the ice to take up construction tools. Prominent team members including Kyle Palmieri, Bo Horvat, Ryan Pulock, Adam Pelech, JG Pageau, and Kyle MacLean worked shoulder-to-shoulder with community volunteers. This hands-on approach allowed the athletes to connect with the residents they represent on the ice.
Kelly Cheeseman, the president of Business Operations for the Islanders, emphasized that such projects provide a unique opportunity for the entire organization, including players and staff, to bond through shared labor and a common purpose. The team views these activities as essential for maintaining a healthy relationship with the community, allowing them to make a tangible impact that lasts far longer than a single game or season.
One of the most inspiring aspects of this project was the child-led design process. Rather than relying on a standard blueprint, the organizers turned to the children of the Cross Island YMCA for guidance. In June, local youth were invited to share their visions, drawings, and ideas for their dream playground, often interacting with the team mascot, Sparky, during the process. Kathryn Lusk, the senior director of field operations for KABOOM!
, highlighted that the specific features of the playground, such as the variety of slides, swings, and a unique spinner, were direct results of the children's requests. This inclusive approach ensures that the facility meets the actual needs and desires of its primary users, fostering a sense of ownership and pride among the local youth.
KABOOM! continues to lead a national movement to eliminate playground inequities, ensuring that every child, regardless of their zip code, has access to a safe and stimulating environment to play. The completed playground is a visual tribute to the team, featuring the iconic blue, orange, and white colors of the New York Islanders, along with the team's logo and themed imagery. The facility was officially opened with a celebratory ribbon-cutting ceremony on Wednesday afternoon.
For the Islanders, whose home rink at UBS Arena is situated just minutes away from the site, this project represents a strategic effort to deepen their roots in the neighborhood. Kyle Palmieri reflected on the importance of this engagement, noting that professional athletes have a responsibility to ingrain themselves in the community and express gratitude to the fans who support them.
By providing a modern and safe space for thousands of annual YMCA visitors, the project ensures a lasting legacy of health and happiness for the youth of New York
